task.title: Separate the non-retriable terminal failure reasons from the retriable ones
task.requested_change: Give the terminal failure reason vocabulary a severity split, so that a non-retriable terminal failure reason is recorded as a distinct reason from a retriable gate failure instead of both collapsing into one blanket phase gate failure reason.
task.problem_statement: The terminal failure reason an orchestrator records at the end of a run flattens every gate failure into a single blanket phase gate failure reason, including the failures execution-report.js itself classifies as non-retriable — an upheld advocate dissent and an evidence integrity breach. A retriable failure and a non-retriable one are then indistinguishable in run_manifest.failure_reason, so a reader cannot tell a run worth retrying from a run that must be quarantined without re-deriving the severity by parsing gate detail strings.
acceptance_criteria: The terminal failure reason vocabulary documents, for every reason, whether that reason is retriable or non-retriable, and the severity is stated in the same table the reason is defined in.
An upheld advocate dissent terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
An evidence integrity breach terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
The severity of a terminal failure reason is sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes, not re-derived by an orchestrator parsing gate detail strings.
non_goals: Changing the decision or exit code vocabulary of execution-report.js.
Adding a new gate, a new phase, or a new validator.
constraints: The failure reason vocabulary must stay a closed enum — no free-text terminal reason.
Existing recorded failure reasons must keep their current meaning, so a reason may be added but never silently redefined.
The orchestrator must source the retriable/non-retriable severity, never re-derive it by parsing gate detail prose.
The parity fixture corpus must keep scoring the same decision and exit code.
